questions.question: The largest fluid compartment of the body is the:

options.D: Intracellular fluid (about two-thirds of total body water)

questions.explanation: Total body water is about 60% of body weight in a young man.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Movement of a substance from a region of high concentration to low concentration without energy is:
questions.explanation: Facilitated diffusion uses carrier proteins but no ATP.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Osmosis is the movement of:

options.B: Water across a semipermeable membrane towards the higher solute concentration

questions.explanation: Osmotic pressure depends on the number of particles.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A red blood cell placed in a hypotonic solution will:
questions.explanation: In hypertonic solution it crenates.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Primary active transport is exemplified by the:
questions.explanation: Secondary active transport uses the sodium gradient (e.g. SGLT).
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The maintenance of a relatively constant internal environment is called:
questions.explanation: Described by Claude Bernard and Walter Cannon.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The release of neurotransmitter at a synapse depends on the entry of:

options.A: Calcium ions into the presynaptic terminal

questions.explanation: Calcium triggers vesicle fusion.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: An inhibitory postsynaptic potential is produced by:

options.A: Increased chloride or potassium conductance causing hyperpolarisation

questions.explanation: GABA and glycine are inhibitory transmitters.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Smooth muscle contraction is initiated by calcium binding to:
questions.explanation: No troponin in smooth muscle.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Cardiac muscle cannot be tetanised because of its:
questions.explanation: Ensures relaxation and filling between beats.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Gamma motor neurones innervate the:

options.A: Intrafusal muscle fibres of the muscle spindle

questions.explanation: They adjust spindle sensitivity (gamma loop).
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Renshaw cells in the spinal cord mediate:
questions.explanation: They use glycine.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: A high MCV with low haemoglobin indicates:
questions.explanation: Microcytic anaemia has a low MCV.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The normal haematocrit in an adult male is about:
questions.explanation: Female 36–46%.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The erythrocyte sedimentation rate is increased in:
questions.explanation: ESR is a non-specific marker of inflammation.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The extrinsic pathway of coagulation is initiated by:

options.D: Tissue factor (factor III) released from damaged tissue

questions.explanation: Measured by prothrombin time; intrinsic by APTT.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Heparin acts as an anticoagulant by:
questions.explanation: Warfarin acts by antagonising vitamin K.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: T lymphocytes mature in the:
questions.explanation: B cells mature in the bone marrow.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Vagal stimulation of the SA node causes:
questions.explanation: Sympathetic stimulation increases heart rate via noradrenaline.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Isovolumetric contraction occurs when:

options.D: All valves are closed and ventricular pressure rises

questions.explanation: It follows closure of the AV valves.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The normal ejection fraction of the left ventricle is about:
questions.explanation: EF = stroke volume / end-diastolic volume.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Venous return is aided by:

options.A: The skeletal muscle pump, respiratory pump and venous valves

questions.explanation: Exercise increases venous return.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The vasomotor centre is located in the:
questions.explanation: It maintains vasomotor tone.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Fluid leaves the capillary at the arterial end because:

options.C: Hydrostatic pressure exceeds plasma oncotic pressure

questions.explanation: At the venous end oncotic pressure predominates (Starling forces).
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Pulse pressure is:

options.B: The difference between systolic and diastolic pressure
options.C: The sum of systolic and diastolic

questions.explanation: Normally about 40 mmHg.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Lung compliance is:

options.A: The change in lung volume per unit change in pressure

questions.explanation: Reduced in fibrosis and increased in emphysema.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The Haldane effect describes:

options.A: Right shift of the dissociation curve
options.C: Increased CO₂ carrying capacity of deoxygenated blood

questions.explanation: Deoxyhaemoglobin binds CO₂ and H⁺ better.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Most carbon dioxide is transported in the blood as:
questions.explanation: About 70% as bicarbonate.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: In the lung, a low alveolar PO₂ causes:

options.A: Local pulmonary vasoconstriction, diverting blood to better ventilated areas

questions.explanation: Sustained global hypoxia causes pulmonary hypertension.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: At the apex of the lung in an upright person the ventilation–perfusion ratio is:
questions.explanation: Perfusion increases more steeply down the lung than ventilation.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The Hering–Breuer inflation reflex:

options.A: Inhibits inspiration when lung stretch receptors are stimulated

questions.explanation: Vagal afferents.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The countercurrent multiplier mechanism of the loop of Henle:

options.A: Creates a hypertonic medullary interstitium for concentrating urine

questions.explanation: Vasa recta act as the exchanger.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Aldosterone acts on the distal tubule and collecting duct to:

options.A: Increase sodium reabsorption and potassium excretion

questions.explanation: Secreted by the adrenal zona glomerulosa.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The micturition reflex centre is located in the:
questions.explanation: Pelvic parasympathetic nerves cause detrusor contraction.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The most important buffer system in the extracellular fluid is the:
questions.explanation: Henderson–Hasselbalch equation relates pH to bicarbonate and CO₂.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Gastrin stimulates:
questions.explanation: Secreted by G cells of the antrum.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Cholecystokinin causes:

options.A: Gallbladder contraction and release of pancreatic enzymes

questions.explanation: Released by I cells in response to fat.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Secretin stimulates the pancreas to secrete:
questions.explanation: Released from duodenal S cells in response to acid.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The defecation reflex is mediated through:
questions.explanation: Voluntary control through the external anal sphincter (pudendal nerve).
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The adrenal medulla secretes mainly:
questions.explanation: Phaeochromocytoma is a tumour of the medulla.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Oxytocin is released from the:
questions.explanation: Causes uterine contraction and milk ejection.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Prolactin secretion is under the inhibitory control of:
questions.explanation: Dopamine antagonists raise prolactin.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Glucagon raises blood glucose by:

options.D: Stimulating glycogenolysis and gluconeogenesis in the liver

questions.explanation: Secreted by alpha cells of the pancreas.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The sympathetic nervous system causes:

options.B: Increased heart rate, bronchodilatation and pupil dilatation

questions.explanation: Parasympathetic: rest and digest.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The basal ganglia are mainly concerned with:

options.B: Initiation and smooth control of movement

questions.explanation: Lesions cause tremor, rigidity or chorea.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The cerebellum is primarily responsible for:
questions.explanation: Lesions cause ataxia on the same side.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: Upper motor neurone lesions produce spasticity mainly because of:

options.B: Loss of descending inhibition of the stretch reflex

questions.explanation: Hyperactive gamma loop.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The organ of Corti is located in the:
questions.explanation: Hair cells transduce sound.
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)

questions.question: The sensation of taste is carried by the facial, glossopharyngeal and:
questions.explanation: Anterior two-thirds of the tongue: facial (chorda tympani).
questions.sourceBook: A.K. Jain, Textbook of Physiology; Guyton & Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology (chapter-level reference)
